cards.explanation: The answer is True. After He had dismissed the crowds, Jesus “…went up on the mountain by Himself to pray.” (Matthew 14:23). He heads up to be alone and pray. Friends, I'd have gone straight for a nap.

The answer is wind. The text says the boat was “…buffeted by the waves because the wind was against it.” (Matthew 14:24). Rowing into a wind like that is like walking into a gust with your umbrella open. You push forward and it pushes right back.

The answer is walking on the sea. “…Jesus went out to them, walking on the sea.” (Matthew 14:25). He's out on top of the water, headed toward the disciples in their boat. The boat was already far from land by then, and all of it happens during the fourth watch of the night.

The answer is ghost. The disciples say, “It’s a ghost!” and cry out in fear (Matthew 14:26). It's the fourth watch of the night and somebody is walking on the water. Friends, I'm not sure what else I'd have yelled either.

The answer is False. Jesus doesn't wait. “Jesus spoke up at once: ‘Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.’” (Matthew 14:27). The disciples were terrified, and He talked to them right then. I think that's a good dad move.

The answer is that Peter asks Jesus to command him to come on the water. Peter, one of the disciples, says, “Lord, if it is You, command me to come to You on the water” (Matthew 14:28). He doesn't ask for a smoother sea. He asks to come out to Jesus. That's a big ask with the wind blowing like that.

The answer is True. Peter “…got down out of the boat, walked on the water, and came toward Jesus.” (Matthew 14:29). He actually walked on it. Bakers, I'd have stared at that water for an hour before I hopped off on my gold base.

The answer is the strength of the wind. “…when he saw the strength of the wind, he was afraid and, beginning to sink, cried out…” (Matthew 14:30). The wind was there the whole time. It was seeing it that hit him. Be honest, friends, I'd have been under the water before he was.

The answer is immediately. “Immediately Jesus reached out His hand and took hold of Peter.” (Matthew 14:31). Peter was beginning to sink when that happened (Matthew 14:30). He had just cried out, “Lord, save me!” (Matthew 14:30). That's what I'd call a quick hand.

The answer is when they climb back into the boat. “…when they had climbed back into the boat, the wind died down.” (Matthew 14:32). That's the moment the text gives for the wind dying down. I think that's worth noticing.

The answers are worshiped and Son. The text says “…those who were in the boat worshiped Him…” (Matthew 14:33). Earlier the disciples were terrified and cried out, “It’s a ghost!” (Matthew 14:26). Then they say, “Truly You are the Son of God!” (Matthew 14:33). I think that's a big change, friends.

The answer is False. They spread the news. The text says the men of Gennesaret, the place where they landed, “…sent word to all the surrounding region.” (Matthew 14:35). Then people brought all the sick to Him. It's like a group chat that never stops buzzing.

The answer is that they beg to just touch the fringe of His cloak. They “…begged Him just to let them touch the fringe of His cloak.” (Matthew 14:36). That's what the people in Gennesaret ask for. I think it's a humble thing to ask.
The answer is True, all of them. “…all who touched Him were healed.” (Matthew 14:36). The text says all, not most and not some. That's the word to hold on to, friends.
